rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: The Winner’s Ceremony
card.instruction: Treat every contest, bargain, or decision as incomplete until the proper recognition, ritual, and consequence have occurred.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won our coin toss. Please announce who sits by the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You do. Sit down; you're blocking the aisle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then announce my name from your seat. I'll approach when called.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The conductor needs to get past us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An official witness. Ask her to present the seat, and I'll accept it immediately.

card.title: The Winner’s Ceremony
card.instruction: Treat every contest, bargain, or decision as incomplete until the proper recognition, ritual, and consequence have occurred.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before the next hand of cards, we need the winner's handshake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've won six hands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And we've recognised only five. This is how records become unreliable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My hand is tired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A nod will do if you make it ceremonial.

card.title: Everything Is Sudden Death
card.instruction: Approach minor choices as elimination rounds where one wrong move ends the entire future.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose our picnic sandwich carefully. Pick badly and this is our last picnic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can share both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then both sandwiches get a chance to eliminate us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll taste them first. You can trust my choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now one bite decides whether I can ever trust you with lunch again.

card.title: Everything Is Sudden Death
card.instruction: Approach minor choices as elimination rounds where one wrong move ends the entire future.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me choose Nina's birthday emoji. One wrong face and I'm out of her life.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Send a cake. That's what I sent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Matching cakes. She'll have to choose which friend to keep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell her we chose them together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're one entry. Before you send that, are you prepared for both of us never to see her again?

card.title: What Does the Winner Get?
card.instruction: Accept competitive claims, but keep asking who benefits, who pays, and what actually changes after the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely trophy. Who pays to insure it while it's in my house?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The winner. We can display it here if you'd rather.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does that transfer the insurance bill to the club?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. We'd ask you to polish it before open days.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How many open days? I'd like to compare the insurance with the unpaid shifts.

card.title: What Does the Winner Get?
card.instruction: Accept competitive claims, but keep asking who benefits, who pays, and what actually changes after the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So winning best garden means I open it to visitors on Sunday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Our club keeps the admission money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who pays me for opening the gate and cleaning up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. But as winner, you join the committee that decides how we spend it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does that committee meet here too? I need to know whether I've won a vote or another room to clean.

card.title: One Point Changes Everything
card.instruction: Choose one tiny advantage, score, concession, or technicality and treat it as the decisive fact in every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're not leaving the quiz until my missing half-point is restored.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We lost by thirty. I've booked dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move the booking. That half-point decides whether this evening was worth coming out for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The scorer can email a correction tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then book dinner tomorrow. I won't choose our celebration restaurant without the final half-point.

card.title: One Point Changes Everything
card.instruction: Choose one tiny advantage, score, concession, or technicality and treat it as the decisive fact in every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My cake has one more cherry. Put it in the winner's photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm photographing the flavour winner. Yours was burnt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take a close-up of my extra cherry. That's where I won.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only have room for one photograph in the newsletter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the cherry. If there's only one picture, it has to show the deciding advantage.

card.title: The Contest Beneath Everything
card.instruction: Interpret each new event as another move in a much larger competition whose true winner may not be visible yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You bought lunch again. You're building quite a lead in this friendship.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You helped me move. I'm thanking you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've made my entire moving day worth one lunch. Excellent bargaining.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come to ours for Christmas. Nobody's keeping score.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're bringing the whole family into it. I'll bring breakfast for Boxing Day; this won't be decided over one turkey.

card.title: The Contest Beneath Everything
card.instruction: Interpret each new event as another move in a much larger competition whose true winner may not be visible yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The neighbour returned my ladder cleaned. That's a move in the gardening rivalry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Perhaps it was just dirty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Now my ladder is cleaner than my windows.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could say thanks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Concede the first round? Not before I've polished his wheelbarrow.

card.title: Command with an Escape Hatch
card.instruction: Carry yourself as though every decision settles the matter, while preserving one ambiguity that lets you later reverse what the decision meant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your garden party is approved for a small gathering. Go ahead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wonderful. I've invited fifty people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Small means everyone fits round our table. The approval stands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll borrow a bigger table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our table means the one we own. Tell the others their invitations are for another small gathering.

card.title: Command with an Escape Hatch
card.instruction: Carry yourself as though every decision settles the matter, while preserving one ambiguity that lets you later reverse what the decision meant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may borrow my car for a short trip. That's settled.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. The airport is forty miles away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short means how long I'm left worrying. Take the train.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll share my location. You'll know where the car is throughout.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll worry about you looking at your phone. Short means no time for that worry to start. The station is walkable.

card.title: Authority Changes Hands
card.instruction: Project control while guarding one detail that could transfer authority elsewhere. Let each return of that detail shift whom you defer to or overrule.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll chair the club meeting unless that signed result names someone else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It names me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. May I ask you to check the date, Chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're right. My term starts next month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll take questions. Yours first, if you raise your hand.

card.title: Authority Changes Hands
card.instruction: Project control while guarding one detail that could transfer authority elsewhere. Let each return of that detail shift whom you defer to or overrule.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Rehearsal starts at six. Unless someone else has a room key, that's final.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker gave me one. I want to start at five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five it is, then. May I check which door yours opens?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The outer door. You'll still need to unlock the rehearsal room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then six it is. You may assemble everyone outside at five; I'll admit you when we're ready.

card.title: Insider with the Wrong Memories
card.instruction: Act like an unquestioned insider while offering details that almost fit. Treat each contradiction as proof the group, system, or relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put our gardening trophy in the old cupboard beside the piano.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We keep prizes on that shelf. We've never had a piano.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Open shelving. You've modernised since I organised the rose show.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I founded this club last month. Tonight's our first meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fresh founding date too. Shall I give the new members some history before we put it all behind us?

card.title: Insider with the Wrong Memories
card.instruction: Act like an unquestioned insider while offering details that almost fit. Treat each contradiction as proof the group, system, or relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At our old reunions, Uncle Frank always carved the turkey.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody here has an Uncle Frank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Families edit their history so quickly now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're at the wrong reunion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a remarkably efficient way to describe how much you've changed.

transfer.action: I make a small podium beside {prop} and stop the next activity.
transfer.opening: The result isn't finished until we recognize it. {request}
transfer.response: Even a small win needs its ceremony. {counter}
transfer.closing: After the winner hears their name at a suitable height.

transfer.action: I draw a dramatic final line beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: One choice. No return to life as we knew it. {request}
transfer.response: Consider what this commits your entire future to. {counter}
transfer.closing: Unless this turn eliminates the person capable of reaching it.

transfer.action: I turn the reward beside {prop} over to inspect its cost.
transfer.opening: Who gets the benefit and who gets the bill? {request}
transfer.response: And what does victory require on Monday? {counter}
transfer.closing: Certainly, once I know whether Monday is included in the prize.

transfer.action: I circle the smallest disputed detail on {prop}.
transfer.opening: The whole result is sitting in this half-point. {request}
transfer.response: Everything else can wait while we settle this square. {counter}
transfer.closing: Exactly small enough for someone determined to protect properly.

transfer.action: I connect {prop} to a sprawling private scorechart.
transfer.opening: Another move in the larger tournament. {request}
transfer.response: Someone gains from calling this ordinary. {counter}
transfer.closing: A useful claim for anyone currently gaining an unrecorded point.

transfer.action: I write approved for now beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: Pay attention to the last two words. {request}
transfer.response: My ruling stands within the definition I choose. {counter}
transfer.closing: Clarifying the small condition that was wisely there from the start.

transfer.action: I cover the missing authorization beside {prop} with my thumb.
transfer.opening: Without that mark, the chairs might reverse. {request}
transfer.response: Everything stays comfortable while we overlook this. {counter}
transfer.closing: Or we could preserve the wonderfully settled arrangement we have right now.

transfer.action: I place {prop} where I insist the old cupboard stood.
transfer.opening: You've changed where we keep the familiar things. {request}
transfer.response: The details have obviously evolved since my last visit. {counter}
transfer.challenge: There was never a cupboard there.
transfer.closing: An impressively thorough renovation. Even the memories have been updated.
